findings.claim: The plan's Intent and row r2's behavior said the change does not re-register the job, but Nomad recorded version 19.

verdict.text: The plan's Intent and row r2 now match what happened on the cluster: the apply sent an identical spec to Nomad again, Nomad recorded a new version and ran a deployment, and the running allocation was updated in place without a restart.
The code tree has not changed since round 1, which passed on every other point, so this round passes.

Plan Intent, lines 28-31 of /home/vscode/workspace/.loop/plans/bifrost-ready-detach/README.md, now say: "The provider still re-registers an identical spec, so Nomad records a new job version and a deployment, but the running allocation is updated in place, not restarted." That matches `nomad job history -p -version 19 bifrost` (no diff against 18) and allocation 3e1235b1 running at version 19, both seen in round 1.

Row r2's behavior in rows.json, and the generated eval README line 22, now read "...shows no jobspec change for the bifrost job; the apply re-registers an identical spec, and the running allocation is updated in place, not restarted or replaced." Its fails_when is unchanged and was still not triggered.
Tree: `git diff HEAD --stat` in the worktree still shows only the round-1 changes to services.tf (+5) and test_bifrost_version.py (+10).
No checklist lines were printed for this round.
The new wording in the plan's Intent (lines 28-31) and in r2's behavior replaces the false "does not re-register" claim with an accurate one.
The plan's Outcome line still says "a plan shows no change to the running job".
Read as "the allocation is not restarted", that is still true, and it was not part of f1, so I raise nothing.
